chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted (as a continuous chain) that As-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said:

Indeed, the bearers of the Throne are eight: one of them is in the form of a son of Adam, who asks God for the daily bread of Adam's offspring; the second is in the form of a rooster, who asks God for the daily bread for birds; the third is in the form of a lion, who asks God for the daily bread for beasts of prey; and the fourth is in the form of an ox, who asks God for the daily bread for quadrupeds. The ox lowered its head since the Children of Israel worshipped the calf, and when the Day of Resurrection comes, they will become eight.
ai.seo_question: Who are the eight bearers of the Throne and what do they look like?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq narrates from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) that the eight bearers of the Divine Throne manifest in four primary forms—human, rooster, lion, and ox—to sustain their respective creations, with the ox lowering its head in shame after the Israelites' worship of the golden calf. This narration highlights the cosmic order and the intimate connection between celestial beings and earthly sustenance, culminating in the multiplication of these forms on the Day of Resurrection to reflect the grandeur of Allah's majesty.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 8-5 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted As-Sadiq (MGB) as having said,

“There are four who will carry God’s Throne. One of them is like a human being who asks God for the daily bread of Adam’s offspring (the people). The second one is like a rooster who asks God for the daily bread for birds. The third one is like a lion who asks God for the daily bread for beasts. The fourth one is like a cowwho asks God for the daily bread for quadrupeds. The cow that carries God’s Threshold has held his head down due to shame, since the Israelites worshipped a calf. The ones who carry God’s Threshold shall be eight on the Resurrection Day.”
